user_input: Implement the user's requested Sentinel banking fraud intelligence project in the existing workspace `C:\Banking-Fraud-Detection`, preserving the existing React/Vite frontend, Spring Boot Java backend, and Python FastAPI ML service (do not replace the stack). The requested product modules are: (1) Executive Dashboard: total processed, genuine vs fraud, fraud detection rate, amount analysis, trends over time; (2) Dataset Management: upload CSV, validate, process large datasets with Apache Spark, show processing history; (3) Machine Learning Center: train Random Forest and Logistic Regression, compare them, handle class imbalance, show precision/recall/F1/PR-AUC, persist and load trained models; (4) Transaction Monitoring: score individual/batch transactions with fraud probability and risk levels, filter suspicious transactions; (5) Fraud Investigation: list flagged transactions, transaction details, investigation status, export report. Repository facts observed: frontend is React in `frontend/src/App.jsx`; it uploads CSVs to `POST http://localhost:8080/api/datasets` and gets latest saved dashboard metrics from `/api/model-metrics/latest`; backend is Spring Boot under `backend`, has Dataset/Transaction/Prediction/FraudAlert/ModelMetric entities, a dataset upload endpoint that only stores the file and marks status UPLOADED, and prediction import endpoint that imports a pre-scored CSV with hard-coded model name Random Forest. The frontend Alerts page is a placeholder. The Python ML service under `ml-service/app/main.py` currently accepts only labeled `Time,V1..V28,Amount,Class` CSV up to 50k rows, trains a class-weighted LogisticRegression pipeline, saves a joblib model, and returns real held-out metrics; frontend upload does not call it. Thus the current UI's Random Forest metrics can be stale/unrelated. The requested product modules are not fully implemented; deliver an end-to-end implementation matching the requested modules without fake/stub metrics or silent fallbacks. Use Spark for dataset processing in a suitable local development mode, and update dependency manifests/docs as required. Keep CSV compatibility explicit: implement the available credit-card schema as the initial supported format; don't pretend arbitrary CSV schemas work. Make training/model results actual and connected to the UI/DB; provide actual predictions and persist them so dashboard/alerts/investigation surfaces use data. Include input validation, clear errors, persistence, and focused tests. Preserve existing UX and avoid unrelated changes. Work through analyze/design/implementation, honor boundaries/quality gates, and run targeted builds/tests. If an entire module is too large for this turn, complete a coherent vertical slice and report remaining work explicitly rather than adding fake screens.
title: Sentinel Banking Fraud Intelligence — In-Place Feature Expansion

assessment_snapshot.intro: The project is a brownfield, in-place upgrade across a React/Vite frontend, Spring Boot backend, and FastAPI ML service:
bullets: The existing frontend has Dashboard and Alerts areas; dataset upload posts to Spring Boot and the backend currently only stores files.
The backend already defines Dataset, Transaction, Prediction, FraudAlert, and ModelMetric persistence entities.
The ML service currently trains real class-weighted Logistic Regression and returns held-out metrics for the bounded credit-card CSV schema.
The implementation must connect real training, predictions, persistence, dashboard metrics, alerts, and investigation while preserving the existing UX.
Apache Spark local development mode and cross-service boundaries are key delivery risks.

proposed_outcome: Expand the existing React/Vite, Spring Boot, and FastAPI application in place to deliver real fraud-intelligence workflows: Spark-assisted CSV ingestion for the labeled Time,V1..V28,Amount,Class schema, persistable Random Forest and Logistic Regression training comparisons, stored model artifacts and predictions, and populated dashboard, monitoring, and investigation surfaces.
